chunks: I would rather you suffered the punishment for sinning against me, and for your own sin, and became an inmate of Hell. And that is the requital for the unjust.

key_terms.تَبُوءَ: to bear or assume (a burden or sin)

ai.seo_question: What did Jesus say to his disciples regarding their sins and the Hellfire in Surah Al-Ma'idah?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) addresses the Christian claim of his divinity, asserting that he disclaims any share in their error and warns that they will bear the cumulative burden of their own sins and his. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the prophets' purity (Ismah) and their role as clear warners who do not absorb the sins of others, contrasting with the concept of vicarious atonement. The verse concludes by affirming divine justice, identifying this state as the rightful recompense for the unjust.
